summary: D.C. statehood advocates are pursuing multiple strategies to advance their cause, including mobilizing around midterm elections and securing commitments from sympathetic federal lawmakers, while also responding to recent events that they argue demonstrate the need for local autonomy. Recent federal interventions in D.C.—including a takeover and National Guard deployment—have prompted advocates to emphasize how statehood would protect the District from external federal control, and a House committee is currently considering proposals that advocates say would further undermine D.C.'s fiscal independence. Without statehood, D.C. cannot spend its own local tax revenue until Congress approves its budget, and Congress can override any law the District passes.
